findings.issue: The note addresses the operator with a second-person imperative (tú-imperative «deja de esperar»), so it reads as telling the operator to stop waiting for a reply. Per the context sidecar the actor is the agent: dismissing means the agent stops waiting on this ask. The terminal/phone copy for the same English (tui.asks.dismiss.moot_note, relay.ask.dismiss.moot_note) was corrected for exactly this in its own independent audit and names the agent. Root cause is upstream of the translation: the en context sets `tone: "lowercase fragment, imperative"` for this key while its `note` says the agent stops waiting, so a translator following the tone line lands on an operator-addressed imperative. Coder should also change that tone line (e.g. 'lowercase fragment naming what the agent stops doing') so a re-translation does not regress.
findings.proposed: el agente dejará de esperar respuesta

findings.issue: The many arm renders {count} while one/other render #, so 1.000.000 renders as the unformatted '1000000 de mensajes' (verified with the repo's intl-messageformat); the es style guide says '# renders the formatted number'. Reachable only at exact multiples of 10⁶ messages, so user impact is negligible; graded MINOR because it breaks a style-guide rule.
